questions.q: What is the anti-pattern this lesson describes?
options: The database is the one thing not in source control — a live server changed directly, with no file anyone can read as the source of truth
Storing too many stored procedures in a single Git repository
Using Git for application code but not for documentation
Writing SQL scripts with inconsistent formatting
questions.explain: In most shops, app code is versioned but the database is edited directly on a live server, so the 'source of truth' becomes whatever production currently looks like.

questions.q: What does `git blame` show you for a database object file?
options: Which commit last changed each line of the file, and by whom
The current row count of the table the object references
A list of every user who has ever queried the object
The performance execution plan for a stored procedure
questions.explain: git blame attributes each line in a file's current state to the commit (and author) that last changed it.

questions.q: What actually belongs in a database's Git repository?
options: Object definitions — CREATE scripts for tables, views, procedures, and functions
A full export of every table's row data
Only the database's compiled execution plans
Nothing; databases can't be meaningfully version controlled
questions.explain: Source control for a database means the shape and logic of the schema and its code objects, not the data those objects hold.

questions.q: Why is committing row data into Git a bad idea, per this lesson?
options: Git isn't built to store or diff large row-oriented data efficiently, and it's often a compliance problem to commit real customer data
Git has a hard technical limit of 10 rows per commit
SQL Server actively blocks any export of table data
It would make git blame stop working on object files
questions.explain: Both a practical and a compliance concern make data itself the wrong thing to version — only definitions belong in the repo.

questions.q: What is the real payoff of a pull request for a database change, according to this lesson?
options: It creates a review gate — a second set of eyes can look at the change, and say no, before it reaches production
It automatically fixes any syntax errors in the SQL
It replaces the need for a test environment entirely
It guarantees the change will improve query performance
questions.explain: The core value of source control here isn't just history — it's that nothing reaches production without someone else reviewing it first.
